n0cc15dac522.s: Which of the following is a category of the nine-fold land-use classification of India?
n0cc15dac522.x: Current fallows is one of the nine land-use categories. Net irrigated area and the gross measures are not among them.

nef5563d4799.s: Which land-use measure counts a plot once for each crop grown on it?
nef5563d4799.x: Gross cropped area counts repeated cropping, so it is generally larger than net sown area, which counts a plot only once.

n6f31f749058.s: Kharif crops in India are generally sown in:
n6f31f749058.x: Kharif crops are sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested around September–November.

naef66b2e4a9.s: Which of the following is a traditional commercial crop of Andhra Pradesh?
naef66b2e4a9.x: Groundnut, cotton, tobacco and sugarcane are AP's traditional commercial crops; paddy, jowar and ragi are traditional food crops.

n184bd20cc61.s: Which of the following is one of the Planning Commission's agro-climatic regions?
n184bd20cc61.x: Trans-Gangetic Plains is a Planning Commission region; Central Coastal Delta is not, and Godavari and Scarce Rainfall are AP's own zones.

nf92c4db44fb.s: Which of the following was a component of the Agricultural Renewal Action Plan (APPSC Group-II 2017)?
nf92c4db44fb.x: The plan covered soil health, irrigation/water augmentation with demand management, and credit and insurance; boosting capital formation was not a component.

n154835d29ea.s:
Consider the following statements about the Polavaram Project:
1. It has an installed power capacity of 960 MW.
2. It diverts 80 TMC of water to the Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n154835d29ea.x: Polavaram has a 960 MW capacity and diverts 80 TMC of Godavari water to the Krishna; both statements are correct.

ndf61dcf2132.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Water, Land and Trees Act (APWALTA), 2002:
1. Rainwater harvesting structures are mandatory on plots of 200 sq m and above.
2. Rainwater harvesting structures are mandatory only on plots of 1,000 sq m and above.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ndf61dcf2132.x: APWALTA requires rainwater harvesting on plots of 200 sq m and above, so statement 2's 1,000 sq m threshold is wrong.

n629a6e0dea3.s: Which of the following is a stage-of-extraction category used in the Central Ground Water Board assessment?
n629a6e0dea3.x: The CGWB categories are Safe, Semi-critical, Critical, Over-exploited and Saline; 'adequately exploited' is not one of them.

n0ae1beb5304.s: Which of the following is a component of Command Area Development?
n0ae1beb5304.x: Field channels, drains, land levelling and Water Users' Associations are components of Command Area Development.

n7510f230e43.s:
Consider the following statements about irrigation efficiency:
1. Drip irrigation is about 90% efficient.
2. Flood or basin surface irrigation is about 30–50% efficient.
3. Flood irrigation is more water-efficient than drip irrigation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n7510f230e43.x: Drip (about 90%) is far more efficient than flood/basin irrigation (30–50%), so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: Agriculture's approximate share in India's GVA (Economic Survey 2025-26) is:
new.x: Agriculture contributes about 18% of GVA, nearly one-fifth of national income, though it employs 46.1% of workers.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a role of agriculture in the Indian economy?
o: Supplying raw material such as cotton and jute to industry
Contributing the largest share of GVA
new.x: Agriculture supplies raw material, food security and exports, but its GVA share (~18%) is far below its employment share, not the largest.

new.s: In 2024-25, horticulture output in India was about 367.72 MT. How did it compare with foodgrains?
o: It was less than half of foodgrains
It passed foodgrains output of 357.73 MT
It was a quarter of foodgrains output
new.x: Horticulture output (367.72 MT) overtook foodgrains (357.73 MT) in 2024-25.

new.s: India's net sown area in 2021-22 was about:
new.x: Net sown area was 141 Mha (42.8% of geographical area); 219.16 Mha is the gross cropped area.

new.s: Cropping intensity is calculated as:
new.x: Cropping intensity = gross cropped area ÷ net sown area × 100, about 155.4% for India in 2021-22.

new.s: Which is the largest land-use category in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Net area sown (36.29%) is AP's largest category, followed by forests (22.63%).

new.s: Which is the smallest land-use category in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Miscellaneous tree crops cover only 0.94% of AP, the smallest category; culturable waste is 2.47%.

new.s: India's net irrigated area in 2021-22 was about:
new.x: Net irrigated area was 77.9 Mha; 120.3 Mha is the gross irrigated area.

new.s: After tubewells, which was the second-largest contributor to India's net irrigated area in 2021-22?
new.x: Canals contributed 24.7%, second to tubewells (47.3%); tanks were only 2.8%.

new.s: Women-operated holdings formed what share of operational holdings in the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
new.x: Women-operated holdings rose from 12.8% (2010-11) to 13.9% (2015-16).

new.s: Which State had the largest average operational holding in India as per the Agriculture Census 2015-16?
new.x: Nagaland had the largest average operational holding in 2015-16.

new.s: As per the 11th Agriculture Census (2021-22, provisional), which AP district has the smallest average holding?
new.x: Visakhapatnam has the smallest average holding (0.40 ha); Ananthapuram has the largest (1.62 ha).

new.s: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?
new.x: Watermelon is a Zaid crop; jute is Kharif, while wheat and mustard are Rabi.

new.s: Jute is grown in India as a:
new.x: Jute is a Kharif crop, not Rabi – a common trap.

new.s: Which of the following pulses is a kharif crop?
new.x: Tur/arhar is kharif, whereas gram/chana and peas are rabi.

new.s: Which of the following crops is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: In AP, paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses are grown in both kharif and rabi.

new.s: Foodgrains in India comprise:
new.x: Foodgrains = cereals + pulses; oilseeds are a separate group.

new.s: Rice-wheat expansion during 2015-2025 in States like Punjab, Telangana and Madhya Pradesh was driven mainly by:
new.x: Assured MSP procurement drove rice-wheat expansion in these States.

new.s: Irrigation covers about 67% of rice area in India. What share of pulses area is irrigated?
new.x: Only about 26% of pulses area is irrigated, against 67% of rice area; pulses are largely rainfed.

new.s: After paddy, which is the largest foodgrain group by area in Andhra Pradesh (2024-25)?
new.x: Pulses (11.66 lakh ha) follow paddy (20.97 lakh ha); maize has 3.20 lakh ha.

new.s: Oil palm cultivation is expanding in which AP districts?
new.x: Oil palm is expanding in East Godavari, Eluru and West Godavari.

new.s: Undivided Andhra Pradesh had how many agro-climatic zones?
new.x: Undivided AP had nine zones; the 2017 key had seven and APSES 2024-25 lists six.

new.s: The zonal headquarters (RARS) of the Godavari Zone, known as the 'Rice Bowl', is at:
new.x: Maruteru is the RARS of the Godavari Zone; Nandyal serves Scarce Rainfall and Chintapalle the High Altitude and Tribal Zone.

new.s: The Planning Commission's agro-climatic regionalisation (1989) divided India into:
new.x: The Planning Commission set 15 regions with 72 sub-zones; NARP has 127 zones.

new.s: Which was the first commercial GM crop in India, approved in 2002?
new.x: Bt cotton (2002) is India's only major GM crop; Bt brinjal is under moratorium since 2010.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about GM crops in India:
1. Bt brinjal has been under a moratorium since 2010.
2. GM mustard DMH-11 received GEAC environmental-release approval in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Bt brinjal is under moratorium since 2010, and DMH-11 got the GEAC nod in 2022 (pending in the Supreme Court).

new.s: Tanks provide what share of India's net irrigated area (2021-22)?
new.x: Tanks provide only 2.8%, though they matter in peninsular hard-rock States.

new.s: Under the Culturable Command Area criterion, a minor irrigation project covers:
new.x: Minor projects cover up to 2,000 ha CCA; medium 2,000-10,000 ha; major above 10,000 ha.

new.s: A major irrigation project has a Culturable Command Area of:
new.x: Major projects have CCA above 10,000 ha; 2,000-10,000 ha is medium.

new.s: Since 2016, how many prioritised AIBP projects are funded through NABARD's Long Term Irrigation Fund?
new.x: 99 prioritised AIBP projects (8 in AP) are funded through NABARD's LTIF.

new.s: The Sirhind Canal draws water from the:
new.x: Sirhind Canal in Punjab takes off from the Sutlej at Ropar.

new.s: The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) was launched on:
new.x: PMKSY, the umbrella irrigation scheme, was launched on 1 July 2015.

new.s: Which PMKSY component deals with micro-irrigation?
new.x: Per Drop More Crop covers micro-irrigation (now under PM-RKVY); Har Khet Ko Pani covers assured irrigation and CAD.

new.s: The Micro Irrigation Fund with NABARD has a corpus of:
new.x: The Micro Irrigation Fund has a corpus of Rs 5,000 crore with NABARD.

new.s: The Hariyali guidelines for watershed development came into force from:
new.x: Hariyali guidelines took effect from 1 April 2003.

new.s: Hariyali, IWDP and NWDPRA were merged into which programme in 2008?
new.x: They were merged into the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) under the 2008 common guidelines.

new.s: The Neeranchal National Watershed Project is supported by the:
new.x: Neeranchal is World Bank-aided ($178.5 million), covering nine States including AP and Telangana.

new.s: Under WDC-PMKSY, the Centre-State funding pattern for watershed projects changed from:
new.x: Funding under WDC-PMKSY moved from 90:10 to 60:40.

new.s: As of 2025, India's stage of groundwater extraction is about:
new.x: India's stage of extraction was 60.63% in 2025, up from 60.47% in 2024.

new.s: Component B of PM-KUSUM provides for:
new.x: Component B covers 14 lakh standalone solar pumps (up to 7.5 HP); A is 10,000 MW plants and C is pump solarisation.

new.s: Which State ranks first in micro-irrigation in India?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in micro-irrigation, through APMIP running since 2003.

new.s: Which region accounts for about 64% of the area under the AP Micro Irrigation Project?
new.x: Rayalaseema accounts for 64% of APMIP's 42.25 lakh acres.

new.s: The Polavaram project is built on which river?
new.x: Polavaram is on the Godavari; Galeru-Nagari and Veligonda draw on the Krishna.

new.s: Which of the following AP projects is NOT based on the Krishna?
new.x: Polavaram is a Godavari project; Galeru-Nagari, Veligonda and Nagarjuna Sagar are Krishna-based.

new.s: Polavaram was declared a National Project under the:
new.x: Polavaram is a National Project under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

new.s: How many irrigation tanks does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: AP has 38,862 tanks with an ayacut of 25.60 lakh acres.

new.s: India's per capita annual water availability places it in which category?
new.x: India is already below 1,700 m³ per capita, so it is water-stressed.

new.s: Water, as a subject, falls under which entry of the Constitution?
new.x: Water is Entry 17 of the State List; inter-State rivers are Entry 56 of the Union List.

new.s: Zero or minimum tillage saves irrigation water mainly by:
o: Lowering evaporation and keeping soil moisture
new.x: Less soil disturbance lowers evaporation and keeps soil moisture; more weeds is its drawback.

new.s: Under FAO's Conservation Agriculture, permanent soil cover should be at least:
new.x: Conservation Agriculture asks for permanent soil cover of at least 30%, with minimum disturbance and crop diversification.

new.s: Which irrigation method has an efficiency of about 70-80%?
new.x: Sprinkler is about 70-80% efficient; drip is ~90% and flood/basin 30-50%.

new.s: India's first National Water Policy was adopted in:
new.x: The first NWP came in 1987, revised in 2002 and 2012; NWP-2012 is in force.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the National Water Policy, 2012?
o: Water Regulatory Authority in each State
A single Union authority replacing State institutions
new.x: NWP-2012 proposes a framework law, State regulators, reuse and micro-irrigation incentives, but no single Union authority replacing State institutions.

new.s: The Bureau of Water Use Efficiency (BWUE), set up in October 2022, functions under the:
new.x: BWUE was set up in October 2022 under the National Water Mission.

new.s: Which statement best describes the present status of CADWM?
new.x: CADWM has no new approvals after 2021-22; M-CADWM runs from 2025-26.

new.s: The Command Area Development Programme was launched mainly to:
o: Narrow the gap between irrigation potential created and utilised
new.x: CAD (1974-75) aims to narrow the gap between irrigation potential created and used.

new.s: The National Perspective Plan for river linking was prepared in:
new.x: The NPP dates from 1980; NWDA was set up in 1982 to carry it out.

new.s: Who first proposed linking Indian rivers in the 19th century?
new.x: Sir Arthur Cotton first proposed river linking; K.L. Rao proposed the Ganga-Cauvery link.

new.s: The Godavari-Krishna link of the Godavari-Cauvery proposal starts from:
new.x: The Godavari-Krishna link runs from Inchampalli to Nagarjunasagar.

new.s: The Composite Water Management Index is published by:
new.x: NITI Aayog publishes the CWMI; Gujarat topped it.
